overview.purpose: Persistent, lightweight message queue and background job runner in Go backed by SQLite (and PostgreSQL) inspired by AWS SQS, providing transactional enqueue/dequeue, visibility timeouts, priority ordering, and automatic heartbeat lease extensions without external broker dependencies.
overview.architectureType: Single-table RDBMS-backed task queue leveraging atomic single-statement UPDATE ... RETURNING queries with visibility timeout leases, in-process polling tickers, and serializable transactional semantics.
keyDifferentiators: Zero non-test dependencies; operates directly against standard database/sql interfaces with bring-your-own driver support for SQLite (mattn/go-sqlite3) and PostgreSQL (pgx).
Atomic dequeue without explicit transaction lock steps via single-statement UPDATE goqite SET timeout = ?, received = received + 1 WHERE id = (SELECT id ... LIMIT 1) RETURNING id, body.
First-class ACID integration supporting atomic enqueue/dequeue within caller-provided sql.Tx transactions (enabling transactional outbox patterns).
Autonomous background heartbeat renewal in jobs.Runner that extends visibility leases at 80% (4/5) of the timeout duration to prevent duplicate execution during long-running tasks.
Dual database dialect support (SQLite and PostgreSQL) with strict typing, randomized hex ID defaults (randomblob/pgcrypto), and automatic updated timestamp triggers.

failureModesAndDefenses.failureMode: Worker Crash / Panic During Task Execution
failureModesAndDefenses.detectionMechanism: Absence of Delete call before message timeout expiration timestamp.
failureModesAndDefenses.recoveryAction: Message automatically becomes visible again when now >= timeout and is redelivered to next available worker with incremented received count.

sourceEvidence.observation: If worker goroutine panics or crashes, Delete is bypassed; the message timeout expires and ReceiveTx picks it up on subsequent poll.

historicalOccurrence.rootCause: Unhandled panic could terminate the entire runner process without releasing or recovering in-flight tasks.
historicalOccurrence.fixDescription: Wrapped job execution in deferred recover() handler logging error while relying on visibility timeout for natural re-enqueue.

failureModesAndDefenses.prescribedMitigation: Ensure job handlers are idempotent to tolerate re-execution following crash recovery.

failureModesAndDefenses.failureMode: Visibility Lease Starvation on Long-Running Tasks
failureModesAndDefenses.detectionMechanism: Job execution time exceeding default queue visibility timeout (default 5s).
failureModesAndDefenses.recoveryAction: Runner spawns background goroutine extending message timeout periodically by r.extend every (extend - extend/5) duration.

sourceEvidence.observation: Continuous sleep-and-extend loop calls queue.Extend(jobCtx, m.ID, r.extend) until job context is cancelled upon completion.

historicalOccurrence.rootCause: Long jobs exceeded initial queue timeout, causing other runner instances to receive and execute the same job concurrently.
historicalOccurrence.fixDescription: Implemented auto-extension heartbeat loop inside runner.receiveAndRun.

failureModesAndDefenses.prescribedMitigation: Configure runner Extend duration proportional to expected maximum single-heartbeat network latency.

failureModesAndDefenses.detectionMechanism: Message repeatedly failing or crashing worker until received counter reaches maxReceive.
failureModesAndDefenses.recoveryAction: ReceiveTx query subquery clause received < q.maxReceive permanently suppresses further delivery of the message.

sourceEvidence.observation: Once received == maxReceive, subquery yields no rows and Receive returns nil.

historicalOccurrence.rootCause: Malformed payloads could trigger infinite retry cycles and starve valid tasks.
historicalOccurrence.fixDescription: Enforced configurable maxReceive threshold in NewOpts (default 3).

failureModesAndDefenses.prescribedMitigation: Implement external dead-letter archiving query to extract stranded rows where received >= maxReceive.

failureModesAndDefenses.failureMode: Host Clock Skew Across Distributed Schedulers
failureModesAndDefenses.detectionMechanism: Timezone mismatch or non-UTC local clock causing strftime or timestamp comparisons to evaluate incorrectly against database time.
failureModesAndDefenses.recoveryAction: Explicit conversion to time.Now().UTC() and strict RFC3339 millisecond precision formatting across all query parameters.

sourceEvidence.observation: Enforces rfc3339Milli format ('2006-01-02T15:04:05.000Z07:00') and UTC normalization on all timestamp parameters.

historicalOccurrence.rootCause: Local non-UTC server timestamps in timeout column conflicted with UTC default timestamps generated by SQLite strftime triggers.
historicalOccurrence.fixDescription: Updated all time.Now() calls to time.Now().UTC() across queue operations.

failureModesAndDefenses.prescribedMitigation: Maintain NTP synchronization across all application nodes and database servers.

failureModesAndDefenses.detectionMechanism: database/sql returning 'database is locked' (SQLITE_BUSY) under concurrent transactions.
failureModesAndDefenses.recoveryAction: Testing harness and documentation mandate WAL mode (_journal=WAL), busy timeout (_timeout=5000), single connection limit (SetMaxOpenConns(1)), and runner backoff sleep (time.Sleep(time.Second)) on receive errors.

sourceEvidence.observation: Runner sleeps 1s on non-cancellation receive errors to avoid hammering database under lock contention.

historicalOccurrence.rootCause: Concurrent test suites and parallel benchmarks timed out under unconfigured SQLite concurrency.
historicalOccurrence.fixDescription: Configured WAL journal mode, busy timeouts, and added retry headroom in test fixtures.

failureModesAndDefenses.prescribedMitigation: For multi-process or high-throughput write workloads, configure WAL mode and busy_timeout=5000 on SQLite connections, or migrate to PostgreSQL flavor.

historicalEvolution.rootCause: Timeout calculations used local host timestamps whereas database created/updated timestamps were stored in UTC ISO8601 strings, leading to premature message dequeuing or delayed execution on non-UTC systems.
historicalEvolution.architecturalFix: Standardized all timeout timestamp generation on time.Now().UTC() and formatted with RFC3339 millisecond precision.

evidence.observation: Replaced local time formatting with time.Now().UTC().Add(...) and timeout.Format(rfc3339Milli).

historicalEvolution.rootCause: Queue only supported pure FIFO delivery order, preventing urgent background jobs from bypassing backlog of normal tasks.
historicalEvolution.architecturalFix: Added priority integer column to goqite table, created composite index (queue, priority desc, created), updated ReceiveTx subquery to ORDER BY priority DESC, created LIMIT 1, and expanded jobs.Create signature to accept full goqite.Message.

evidence.observation: Added priority integer not null default 0 and index goqite_queue_priority_created_idx.

historicalEvolution.rootCause: Goqite SQL statements and schema were hardcoded to SQLite-specific syntax (strftime, ?, randomblob), precluding use in enterprise PostgreSQL deployments.
historicalEvolution.architecturalFix: Introduced SQLFlavor enum (SQLFlavorSQLite, SQLFlavorPostgreSQL) in NewOpts, implemented parameterized query branching ($1 vs ? and timestamptz vs text), and created schema_postgres.sql with pgcrypto.

evidence.observation: Added switch q.flavor in SendAndGetIDTx, ReceiveTx, ExtendTx, and DeleteTx.

historicalEvolution.rootCause: Jobs taking longer than the default queue visibility timeout were redelivered to other workers while still actively executing, causing duplicate concurrent execution.
historicalEvolution.architecturalFix: Implemented background heartbeat extension goroutine inside jobs.Runner executing queue.Extend every (extend - extend/5) duration, added panic recovery defer, and added Extend duration option to NewRunnerOpts.

evidence.observation: Spawns goroutine sleeping extend - extend/5 and issuing queue.Extend(jobCtx, m.ID, r.extend) until job completion.

historicalEvolution.rootCause: ReceiveTx executed full table scans as message volume grew large across multiple queues sharing the same goqite table.
historicalEvolution.architecturalFix: Benchmarked and added composite index on (queue, created) [subsequently expanded to (queue, priority desc, created)] to accelerate subquery selection.

evidence.observation: Created index goqite_queue_priority_created_idx on goqite (queue, priority desc, created).

historicalEvolution.rootCause: Application services could not atomically combine business domain database mutations with message enqueue/dequeue in the same database transaction.
historicalEvolution.architecturalFix: Added *Tx method variants (SendTx, SendAndGetIDTx, ReceiveTx, ExtendTx, DeleteTx, CreateTx) and implemented InTx serializable transaction wrapper.

evidence.observation: Implemented InTx with sql.LevelSerializable isolation and automatic rollback on error or panic.

unresolvedContradictionsAndBypasses.claimOrGuarantee: Messages that fail or crash workers are safely managed by the maxReceive limit.
unresolvedContradictionsAndBypasses.contradictionOrBypass: Goqite lacks a Dead-Letter Queue (DLQ) table or automated deletion for poison messages. When received reaches maxReceive, the message is simply ignored by ReceiveTx (due to received < maxReceive), leaving dead rows permanently in the goqite table where they accumulate and degrade index range scan performance over time.
unresolvedContradictionsAndBypasses.evidence: Subquery filter received < ? excludes exhausted messages from dequeue, but no mechanism purges, archives, or moves them to a DLQ table.

unresolvedContradictionsAndBypasses.claimOrGuarantee: Worker has exclusive ownership during task execution.
unresolvedContradictionsAndBypasses.contradictionOrBypass: Extend and Delete do NOT verify a fencing token or lease generation ID. If a worker is delayed by a long GC pause or network stall exceeding its timeout, a second worker dequeues the message. When the first worker wakes up, it can still successfully call Delete(m.ID) or Extend(m.ID), destroying the task while the second worker is mid-execution.
unresolvedContradictionsAndBypasses.evidence: DELETE query is 'delete from goqite where queue = ? and id = ?' with no check on whether received count or timeout timestamp has been mutated by another worker.

unresolvedContradictionsAndBypasses.claimOrGuarantee: Visibility timeouts are strictly deterministic and clock-synchronized.
unresolvedContradictionsAndBypasses.contradictionOrBypass: Time comparisons in ReceiveTx evaluate the Go application server's local time (time.Now().UTC()) against the database row's stored timeout value. In multi-server deployments where application nodes experience clock skew relative to each other or to the central database, messages may be received prematurely or experience unexpected delivery delays.
unresolvedContradictionsAndBypasses.evidence: Query uses parameterized client time (? >= timeout) formatted on the application server rather than database-native now() or strftime('now').

unresolvedContradictionsAndBypasses.claimOrGuarantee: Runner strictly bounds worker concurrency without busy loops or poll thrashing.
unresolvedContradictionsAndBypasses.contradictionOrBypass: When jobCount reaches jobCountLimit, Runner.receiveAndRun releases its read lock and calls time.Sleep(r.pollInterval). It lacks a condition variable, semaphore channel, or worker completion signal, resulting in polling latency when worker slots open and race conditions where multiple goroutines can wake simultaneously.
unresolvedContradictionsAndBypasses.evidence: r.jobCountLock.RLock(); if r.jobCount == r.jobCountLimit { r.jobCountLock.RUnlock(); time.Sleep(r.pollInterval); return; }.

unresolvedContradictionsAndBypasses.claimOrGuarantee: Serializable transactions guarantee completely conflict-free queue operations.
unresolvedContradictionsAndBypasses.contradictionOrBypass: SQLite only supports a single writer in WAL mode. When multiple concurrent producers or consumers call InTx (which sets Isolation: sql.LevelSerializable), transactions serialize on SQLite's database lock, causing SQLITE_BUSY errors if write bursts exceed the 5000ms busy timeout.
unresolvedContradictionsAndBypasses.evidence: InTx enforces sql.LevelSerializable on all transactions, creating lock contention under high-concurrency writes on SQLite backends.

boundaryConditions: Clock jumps or NTP step corrections on application hosts directly alter message visibility horizons because timeout comparisons evaluate Go client time.Now().UTC() rather than database-internal clocks.

Worker partition / GC pause: A worker stalling past its visibility timeout allows a second worker to acquire the task; the first worker then deletes the row upon finishing, aborting the task's guaranteed visibility for the second worker.

Poison pill table bloating: High failure rates lead to thousands of permanent poison rows (received >= maxReceive) that are never deleted, forcing the index scan on (queue, priority desc, created) to traverse increasing numbers of dead rows.
untestedAssumptions: Assumes all distributed Go queue nodes maintain synchronized clocks within sub-millisecond tolerances when querying shared PostgreSQL or network-attached SQLite databases.
Assumes callers will implement custom administrative maintenance jobs to periodically purge or archive exhausted messages (received >= maxReceive).
Assumes database driver connection pools with sql.LevelSerializable will handle lock retries cleanly without inducing application thread starvation under write pressure.
acceptedTradeOffs: Simplicity and zero external dependencies over advanced distributed coordination: Uses single-table atomic UPDATE ... RETURNING instead of distributed lock managers (Redis, etcd, ZooKeeper).
At-least-once delivery over strict exactly-once processing: A worker that crashes, panics, or times out will have its task redelivered upon timeout expiry.
In-process polling over push notifications: Uses periodic tickers (ReceiveAndWait) rather than SQLite commit hooks or PostgreSQL LISTEN/NOTIFY to maintain driver and database neutrality.
